generated.what_happened: US consumer sentiment fell to 46.3 in October from 48.1 in September as persistent inflation, high borrowing costs, and elevated energy prices weighed on households. According to the University of Michigan survey, the decline was led by lower-income consumers, individuals with smaller stock portfolios, and political Independents. Buying conditions deteriorated significantly as mortgage rates reached a three-year high of 7.4% and gas prices remained elevated due to the ongoing Middle East conflict. Additionally, short-term inflation expectations rose to 4.7%, further dampening economic morale ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.
